speaker: narrator
en: Christian walked on alone. Across the field a gentleman came to meet him. His name was Mr Worldly Wiseman.
source: Part I: 'he espied one afar off come crossing over the field to meet him... Mr. Worldly Wiseman' (verify wording)

speaker: worldly_wiseman
en: How now, good fellow, where are you going in this burdened manner?
source: Part I: 'How now, good fellow, whither away after this burdened manner?' (verify wording)

speaker: christian
en: A burdened manner indeed. I am going to yonder wicket gate, where I am told I shall be rid of it.
source: Part I: Christian answers that he goes to the wicket gate (verify wording)

speaker: worldly_wiseman
en: In the village of Morality lives a gentleman named Legality. He can take off such burdens, and the road to his house is smooth.
source: Part I: Worldly Wiseman directs him to Legality in the village of Morality (paraphrase)

speaker: ui
en: Take the smooth road to Morality

speaker: narrator
en: The hill hung over the road. Flashes of fire came out of it, and Christian was afraid it would fall on his head.
source: Part I: the hill 'seemed so high... that Christian was afraid to venture further, lest the hill should fall on his head' (verify wording)

speaker: evangelist
en: What are you doing here, Christian?
source: Part I: 'What doest thou here, Christian?' (verify wording)

speaker: evangelist
en: Did I not show you the way to the little wicket gate? Mr Legality cannot set you free from your burden.
source: Part I: Evangelist explains that Legality cannot ease him of his burden (paraphrase)

speaker: christian
en: Sir, I am sorry. May I yet go back and up to the gate?
source: Part I: Christian asks whether there is hope (paraphrase)

speaker: evangelist
en: The man at the gate will receive you, for he has goodwill for men. Only take heed that you turn not aside again.
source: Part I: 'the man at the gate will receive thee, for he has goodwill for men; only... take heed that thou turn not aside again' (verify wording)

speaker: sign
en: Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life.

speaker: sign
en: Arrows fly from the castle beyond the wall. When you see the glint, shelter behind a rock.

speaker: christian
en: May I now enter here? Will he within open to sorry me, though I have been an undeserving rebel?
source: Part I: Christian's verse at the gate (verify wording)

speaker: goodwill
en: Who is there? Where do you come from, and what would you have?
source: Part I: Goodwill's question at the gate (verify wording)

speaker: goodwill
en: I am willing with all my heart. We make no objections against any.
source: Part I: 'I am willing with all my heart'... 'We make no objections against any' (verify wording)

speaker: narrator
en: As Christian stepped in, Goodwill gave him a pull, for arrows fly from that castle at all who come up to this gate.
source: Part I: Goodwill pulls him in because of Beelzebub's castle and its arrows (paraphrase)
